book.title: A Christmas Carol · Stave 2 — The First of the Three Spirits
book.author: Charles Dickens, A Christmas Carol (1843)

cast.name: Scrooge
cast.role: protagonist — cold, miserly old man who is redeemed
cast.canonical: a bent thin miserly old man with a sharp pointed nose, shrivelled frowning face and thin lips, in a long shabby dark tailcoat, carrying a cane
cast.anchor: a bent thin old man, pointed nose, hard frown, shabby dark tailcoat + cane

cast.name: Ghost of Christmas Past
cast.role: first of the three spirits — memory
cast.canonical: a small luminous spirit that seems both a child and an old person, with long white hair and a bright flame of light springing from its head, in a pure white tunic trimmed with summer flowers, holding a cap shaped like a candle-extinguisher
cast.anchor: small glowing child-old spirit, white tunic, a flame from its crown, extinguisher-cap

cast.name: Fezziwig
cast.role: Scrooge's jovial old master (in Christmas Past)
cast.canonical: a jovial rotund old gentleman with a round beaming face under a big Welsh wig, a comfortable waistcoat and shiny buckled shoes
cast.anchor: rotund beaming old master, big Welsh wig, buckled shiny shoes

cast.name: Belle
cast.role: Scrooge's former fiancee, in Christmas Past
cast.canonical: a gentle graceful young woman with a soft kind face and hair in simple ringlets, in a plain modest early-Victorian dress and shawl
cast.anchor: gentle young woman, simple ringlets, plain modest dress and shawl

panels.scene: the bent sharp-nosed old miser in a nightcap sitting bolt upright in his curtained bed at midnight as a burst of light floods the room and an unseen hand draws back the bed-curtains

teen.narration: THE CLOCK STRIKES ONE. THE FIRST SPIRIT COMES.

bubbles.text: a deep, dull, hollow, melancholy ONE
Light flashed up in the room upon the instant, and the curtains of his bed were drawn
Was it a dream or not?

panels.scene: a small luminous child-yet-aged spirit with long white hair and a bright jet of clear light springing from the crown of its head, in a pure white tunic with a holly sprig, holding a candle-extinguisher cap, beside the startled old miser in his nightcap

teen.narration: A FIGURE BOTH CHILD AND OLD, GLOWING WITH LIGHT.

bubbles.text: like a child: yet not so like a child as like an old man
from the crown of its head there sprung a bright clear jet of light
It held a branch of fresh green holly in its hand
It wore a tunic of the purest white

panels.scene: close on the glowing white-tunic spirit with the flame at its crown speaking gently to the wary old miser, the extinguisher-cap under its arm

teen.narration: IT IS THE GHOST OF CHRISTMAS PAST.

bubbles.speaker: PAST
bubbles.text: I am the Ghost of Christmas Past.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Long Past?

bubbles.speaker: PAST
bubbles.text: No. Your past.
The voice was soft and gentle.

panels.scene: the glowing spirit clasping the old miser's arm and drawing him toward a bedroom wall, the two of them beginning to pass straight through it, the miser in nightcap and slippers

teen.narration: IT TAKES HIS HAND AND LEADS HIM OUT.

bubbles.speaker: PAST
bubbles.text: Rise! and walk with me!
they passed through the wall, and stood upon an open country road
The grasp, though gentle as a woman's hand, was not to be resisted.

panels.scene: a clear cold snowy country road with fields on either side, the old miser in his nightcap and gown clasping his hands in wonder as he recognises his boyhood home, the glowing spirit beside him
panels.composition: wide, back to his boyhood country

teen.narration: THEY STAND WHERE SCROOGE WAS A BOY.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: I was bred in this place. I was a boy here!
a thousand odours floating in the air, each one connected with a thousand thoughts

bubbles.speaker: PAST
bubbles.text: Your lip is trembling

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: I could walk it blindfold

panels.scene: merry country boys on shaggy ponies and in carts trotting down the snowy lane shouting to one another, the old miser and the glowing spirit watching them pass like ghosts
panels.composition: wide, shadows of a merrier past

teen.narration: MERRY BOYS PASS — SHADOWS THAT CANNOT SEE THEM.

bubbles.speaker: PAST
bubbles.text: These are but shadows of the things that have been

bubbles.speaker: PAST
bubbles.text: They have no consciousness of us.
the crisp air laughed to hear it!
The jocund travellers came on

panels.scene: a long bare cold schoolroom, a single lonely small boy reading alone at a desk by a feeble fire, while the old miser sits weeping on a bench watching his forgotten childhood self

teen.narration: A LONELY BOY, LEFT ALONE AT SCHOOL AT CHRISTMAS.

bubbles.speaker: PAST
bubbles.text: A solitary child, neglected by his friends, is left there still.
wept to see his poor forgotten self as he used to be

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Poor boy!
The Spirit touched him on the arm, and pointed to his younger self

panels.scene: a joyful little girl in a bonnet darting into the bare schoolroom to throw her arms round the lonely boy's neck, both radiant, an open door behind
panels.composition: close, little Fan comes for him

teen.narration: HIS LITTLE SISTER FAN COMES TO TAKE HIM HOME.

bubbles.speaker: FAN
bubbles.text: I have come to bring you home, dear brother!

bubbles.speaker: FAN
bubbles.text: Home, for good and all. Home, for ever and ever.

bubbles.speaker: YOUNG SCROOGE
bubbles.text: You are quite a woman, little Fan!
putting her arms about his neck, and often kissing him

panels.scene: a warm warehouse counting-house, a jovial rotund old master in a big Welsh wig laughing behind a very high desk, the old miser pointing in delight, the glowing spirit near

teen.narration: NEXT: THE WAREHOUSE OF JOLLY OLD FEZZIWIG.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Why, it's old Fezziwig! Bless his heart; it's Fezziwig alive again!

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Was I apprenticed here!
sitting behind such a high desk

panels.scene: the rotund Welsh-wig master clapping his hands and springing down from his high desk with wonderful agility, calling for the shutters up and the floor cleared for a party

teen.narration: HE CLOSES SHOP FOR A CHRISTMAS EVE BALL.

bubbles.speaker: FEZZIWIG
bubbles.text: No more work to-night. Christmas Eve, Dick. Christmas, Ebenezer!

bubbles.speaker: FEZZIWIG
bubbles.text: Clear away, my lads, and let's have lots of room here!

bubbles.speaker: FEZZIWIG
bubbles.text: before a man can say Jack Robinson!
skipping down from the high desk, with wonderful agility

panels.scene: a bright warm warehouse turned ballroom, a fiddler up on the high desk, Mrs Fezziwig one vast smile, many couples dancing in joyful rows under warm lamplight and holly

bubbles.text: In came a fiddler with a music-book
In came Mrs. Fezziwig, one vast substantial smile.
Away they all went, twenty couple at once
In came the three Miss Fezziwigs, beaming and lovable.

panels.scene: the rotund Welsh-wig master and his substantial smiling wife dancing a lively reel in the middle of the floor, his buckled shoes and shining calves flashing, everyone delighted

teen.narration: FEZZIWIG AND HIS WIFE LEAD THE DANCE.

bubbles.text: A positive light appeared to issue from Fezziwig's calves.
They shone in every part of the dance like moons.
he appeared to wink with his legs, and came upon his feet again without a stagger

panels.scene: the glowing spirit and the old miser standing aside from the fading ball, the miser earnestly defending his old master, the light on the Ghost's head burning clear
panels.composition: close, the lesson of small kindness

teen.narration: THE SPIRIT TESTS WHAT SUCH KINDNESS IS WORTH.

bubbles.speaker: PAST
bubbles.text: A small matter... to make these silly folks so full of gratitude.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: The happiness he gives, is quite as great as if it cost a fortune.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: He has the power to render us happy or unhappy

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: to make our service light or burdensome; a pleasure or a toil

panels.scene: a gentle young woman with simple ringlets in a plain mourning dress with tears in her eyes, sitting beside a younger, harder-eyed man in whose face greed is beginning to show, by candlelight
panels.composition: close, Belle and the young Scrooge

teen.narration: YEARS LATER — SCROOGE'S YOUNG SWEETHEART, BELLE.

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: Another idol has displaced me
an eager, greedy, restless motion in the eye

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: It matters little... To you, very little.
sat by the side of a fair young girl in a mourning-dress

panels.scene: the gentle ringletted young woman speaking sadly but steadily to the greedy-eyed young man, who looks away, unable to deny it

teen.narration: SHE NAMES WHAT HAS REPLACED HER LOVE.

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: A golden one.

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: the master-passion, Gain, engrosses you

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: You fear the world too much

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: All your other hopes have merged into the hope of being beyond the chance of its sordid reproach

panels.scene: the gentle ringletted young woman gently releasing the young man from their engagement, sorrowful but resolved, turning to leave him

teen.narration: BELLE RELEASES HIM — FOR THE MAN HE ONCE WAS.

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: I release you. With a full heart, for the love of him you once were.

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: May you be happy in the life you have chosen!

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: I would gladly think otherwise if I could

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: the memory of what is past half makes me hope you will

panels.scene: a warm firelit parlour years on, the same woman now a comely matron laughing among her many boisterous children and loving husband by the Christmas fire, the old miser watching in aching sorrow
panels.composition: wide, the family Scrooge never had

teen.narration: BELLE, YEARS ON — HAPPY WITH THE FAMILY SCROOGE LOST.

bubbles.speaker: HUSBAND
bubbles.text: Quite alone in the world, I do believe.
his sight grew very dim indeed

bubbles.speaker: HUSBAND
bubbles.text: I saw an old friend of yours this afternoon.
been a spring-time in the haggard winter of his life

panels.scene: the anguished old miser wrestling with the glowing spirit and forcing the great candle-extinguisher cap down over its head, brilliant light streaming out from under the cap onto the ground
panels.composition: close, Scrooge puts out the light

teen.narration: UNABLE TO BEAR MORE, SCROOGE SNUFFS THE SPIRIT OUT.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: show me no more!
he seized the extinguisher-cap
he could not hide the light: which streamed from under it

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Haunt me no longer!
